decisive_spans.text: well-defined mass at the level of the anorectal junction extending into the right ischiorectal fossa

response.rationale: The presence of large, ulcerative lesions and a significant mass at the anorectal junction strongly supports Anal Cancer (D1). While Crohn's disease (D9) is supported by the history of perianal fistula, it does not account for the specific findings of a large mass and ulcerative lesions as well as Anal Cancer. Tuberculosis (D3) is contradicted by the histological findings of mucinous adenocarcinoma.
